PLAN: Restore R953 (0.494), then use the remaining budget only on the TT/TTT subsystem; test a modestly larger side draw for extra C3 recovery, and revert if purity or revenue worsens.
R953 combines the proven 45-stage root with TTT boil-up 0.7. Its five products total $603.1M/yr and cost $386.7M/yr. Root pressure drop 0.3 was decisively bad; dp 0.2 is essential. TTT boil-up 0.6 failed on ethane, 0.8 recovered less C3, and 0.7 is best. The current test raises TT liquid side draw from 0.25 to 0.28: TTS is 97% C3 and TTB contains 4% propane, so a slightly larger draw may recover more C3 while remaining above both 95% blend specifications. This changes only TT and TTT, fitting the three-solve remainder. Preserve R953 as fallback.
